item.text:
**7B.7 Shehbaz Sharif (2024)**  
Overall: **mixed, leaning no**. I found some evidence of reactive probes and disciplinary responses, but the dominant 2024 pattern was state suppression of critics, information control, and weakening of judicial independence. I did **not** find a clean 2024 source showing Sharif personally ordering concealment of a specific illegal/self-serving act; the stronger record is broader institutional obstruction.

**Accepted claims**
- **Pakistan to investigate army’s meddling in judiciary, law minister says** | Reuters via Al Jazeera | 2024-03-28 | https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/3/28/pakistan-to-investigate-armys-meddling-in-judiciary-law-minister-says | After six High Court judges alleged ISI intimidation, the Sharif government said it would form an inquiry commission. This is the clearest positive item: it shows an official, at least nominally independent probe into politically sensitive interference rather than immediate shutdown. | QIDs: 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.2
- **Mohtasib resolves 193,028 complaints, provides relief of Rs 48.98bn** | President of Pakistan | 2024-02-07 | https://president.gov.pk/mohtasib-resolves-193028-complaints-provides-relief-of-rs-4898-billion-2 | The federal ombudsman handled a large volume of complaints and provided relief, showing complaint-handling infrastructure remained active in 2024. This is only weakly tied to Sharif personally, but it is a real counterpoint to total concealment. | QIDs: 7B.7, 7B.6
- **PM orders action over ‘ineffective’ track and trace system** | Dawn | 2024-05-08 | https://www.dawn.com/news/1832117 | Sharif ordered action after an inquiry report found the FBR’s track-and-trace system ineffective. That is a concrete response to a damaging internal finding, not simple suppression of the finding. | QIDs: 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.5
- **Bisham attack: PM Shehbaz orders immediate action against 5 officials for negligence of duty** | Dawn | 2024-04-06 | https://www.dawn.com/news/1826071/bisham-attack-pm-shehbaz-orders-immediate-action-against-5-officials-for-negligence-of-duty | After an inquiry report on the Bisham attack, Sharif ordered disciplinary action against five officials for negligence. This supports a limited pattern of accepting adverse findings and punishing administrative failure rather than burying it. | QIDs: 7B.7, 7B.6
- **PM orders urgent inquiry into Neelum-Jhelum project’s technical fault** | APP | 2024-05-16 | https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-orders-urgent-inquiry-into-neelum-jhelum-projects-technical-fault/ | Sharif ordered an urgent probe into the Neelum-Jhelum technical fault. This is a fact-finding response to failure, though it is still tightly controlled from the top. | QIDs: 7B.7, 7B.6
- **Pakistan’s government curbs judiciary’s power after alleged harassment of MPs** | The Guardian | 2024-10-21 | https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps | The 26th Amendment weakened judicial independence amid allegations of intimidation and abductions of MPs. That is strong evidence of neutralizing courts rather than allowing independent accountability. | QIDs: 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.2
- **Pakistan widening crackdown on dissent** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent | HRW said the government clamped down on dissenting media, the opposition, and NGOs, with pressure that deepened self-censorship and fear. This is strong evidence of state power being used to suppress scrutiny and intimidate critics. | QIDs: 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.2
- **Social media platform X blocked in Pakistan over national security, ministry says** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-04-17 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313 | The interior ministry confirmed it blocked X around the election period on national-security grounds, directly restricting reporting and public monitoring. This is evidence of using state power to limit scrutiny at a politically sensitive time. | QIDs: 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.2
- **Pakistan: New Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest** | Amnesty International | 2024-09-09 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/ | Amnesty said the government rushed through a law that criminalized peaceful assembly and expanded restriction powers. That points to suppression of dissent and public oversight, not protection of independent scrutiny. | QIDs: 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.2
- **Dangerous digital crackdown** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-12 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/12/dangerous-digital-crackdown | HRW said internet throttling, VPN restrictions, and PECA-based controls were expanding by late 2024. This is evidence of a deepening information-control apparatus that can be used to hide misconduct and pressure critics. | QIDs: 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.2
- **Pakistan controversial Punjab Defamation Act signed into law** | Library of Congress | 2024-06-25/26 | https://www.loc.gov/item/global-legal-monitor/2024-06-25/pakistan-controversial-punjab-defamation-act-signed-into-law | Critics said the act created tribunal and platform-suspension powers that could be weaponized against critics and media. This is strong structural evidence of laws that can neutralize scrutiny. | QIDs: 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.2
- **2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Pakistan** | U.S. Department of State via ecoi.net | 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128431.html | The report says the government rarely took credible steps to identify and punish officials who committed abuses, and that PEMRA/PTA/FIA tools were used to pressure media and suppress threatening information. This is broad evidence of accountability avoidance and state-backed concealment. | QIDs: 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.2

**Search gap**
- I did **not** find a reliable 2024 source directly proving Sharif personally ordered concealment of a specific illegal or self-serving act tied to his own assets, campaign finance, or family conflicts.
- The strongest evidence is indirect: media suppression, protest crackdowns, digital controls, judicial weakening, and only a few reactive inquiries/corrective actions.
- So the best-supported reading is **not** that Sharif was wholly transparent, but that he governed in a system that used state power heavily to obstruct scrutiny while occasionally allowing limited probes when pressure was already public.
